A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SGP-Bench and Symbolic Instruction Tuning work. Their text, figures, tables and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material and renamed datasets.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, SIT experiments, a human study in Appendix B, and additional finetuning experiments in Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results and adds qualitative model-response comparisons in Section 3.

M1.justification: The rendering-based benchmark pipeline, caption-derived SIT, LoRA/OFT finetuning, and reverse/mixed SIT procedures remain unchanged. Reverse SIT was already described in v1 Section 7; its earlier introduction in v2 is reorganization.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same SVG, DeepCAD, Fusion360, SketchGraphs, SGP-MNIST and general instruction-tuning benchmark coverage. The CAD subset called 3Drecon. becomes 3Dcomplex without changing its source or composition. The new qualitative cases concern existing tasks.

E2.justification: Yi-1.5-34B is removed from the SGP-MNIST comparison, moving from seven models in v1 Table 3 to six in v2 Table 4. Figures 3–4 introduce o1 qualitative evaluations, including comparison with Llama-3.1-8B and 70B. Table 1 retains its comparator membership.

E3.justification: Appendices A.2, E and F retain the evaluation procedures, prompts, training settings and dataset-size sweeps. The main-text SIT count changes from 55K to 72K, but 72K was already documented in v1 Appendix E, so this does not establish an expanded training budget. Step-by-step prompting also predates the added cases.

E4.justification: v2 Section 3 adds qualitative analyses of CAD reasoning and digit recognition, examining how model responses connect geometric components to answers. The perturbation tests, human/model entropy comparison, dataset-size ablations and LoRA/OFT comparison were already present and remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Human-study agreement statistics and prediction-entropy reporting are unchanged. Neither version introduces repeated-run uncertainty, seed reporting, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 2 changes the original-model accuracy from 46.7 to 46.5 while retaining gains calculated from 46.7 and the appendix's 46.7 baseline. The MNIST table drops Yi's 5.5 result. Section 4.2 corrects the Qwen CAD comparison from 0.560/0.694 to 0.486/0.632, matching the retained Table 1 averages. New qualitative outputs appear, but Table 1, transfer scores and appendix ablation values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The operational definitions of understanding and consistency, and the transformation assumptions, are retained. No mathematical results, proofs or derivations are added; the new reasoning discussions are explanatory.

C1.justification: v2 explicitly promotes improvement in general reasoning in its abstract, contribution list and conclusion, where v1 emphasized generic instruction-following performance. This broadens the framing of the retained transfer results; the central SGP-Bench, SIT and MNIST contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations connecting SIT to interconnected reasoning skills and attributing MNIST difficulty to irregular paths, absent semantic components and digit-thickness loops. Section 5 shifts its limitation discussion from not surpassing GPT-4o to remaining below Llama-3.1-70B. These extend interpretation without new controlled evidence establishing the proposed mechanisms.

D1.justification: Section 4.3 newly documents visual inspection of perturbed renderings. Section 5 aligns its corpus count with the 72K already documented in v1's appendix, but removes the direct Hugging Face link for SIT data in favor of a generic availability statement. Appendix implementation settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 acknowledges Cai et al.'s SVG understanding work and the concurrent VGBench, sharpening its positioning around general graphics programs. It also adds code-training/reasoning references and trims some multimodal literature discussion. The broader related-work coverage remains largely intact.

P1.justification: The abstract is substantially rewritten and the main narrative reorganized. Related work moves from Section 2 into the concluding Section 8, a motivation section is introduced, and the transfer and MNIST sections change order. Several explanations are rewritten and the acknowledgments are omitted.

P2.justification: v2 adds reasoning-response Figures 3–4, clarifies inputs in Figure 1, and combines earlier SIT displays into Figure 10. The MNIST example panel moves to Appendix A.1. The transfer table is reorganized with separate IFEval rows, alongside document-wide typography, header and layout changes.

improvement.justification: v2 more clearly explains what models receive and better acknowledges direct SVG prior work. Its qualitative cases and failure explanations help readers interpret the retained evidence. These are limited gains because quantitative validation is essentially unchanged, and they are partly offset by Table 2's inconsistent baseline/gains and removal of the direct SIT-data link.
